sketches.title: Countertop Coup
sketches.premise: Two kitchen revolutions collide: on each turn, play a kitchen object or force that takes control of the thing before it. The counter becomes a tiny, ruthless kingdom, and the last card that cannot seize power loses.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new standing kitchen thing directly captures, traps, cuts, melts, washes away, blocks, or otherwise controls the previous thing; merely hiding from it, surviving it, or playing a larger copy loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one standing thing and its takeover in one sentence: "I am the lid, clamping shut on the pot." A bigger copy fails: "I am a bigger pot" is just royal bloat, not a coup.
sketches.first_card: I am a raw egg, sitting smugly on the counter.

sketches.title: Recipe Race
sketches.premise: Players build rival recipes one ingredient at a time, but every new ingredient must transform the current dish into a recognizable next stage. If your addition does nothing, ruins the dish without a clear purpose, or merely repeats what is already there, the kitchen declares you useless.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the ingredient plainly changes the standing dish toward a named, edible kitchen result; dodging the dish, merely adding more of the same ingredient, or claiming a figure of speech such as "love cooks it" does not count as a mechanism.
sketches.move_shape: Name an ingredient and its concrete effect: "I am flour, thickening the beaten eggs into batter." A cousin from the same family fails: "I am more flour" thickens only by repetition.
sketches.first_card: A raw potato, peeled and waiting beside the bowl.

sketches.title: Appliance Argument
sketches.premise: Every kitchen appliance gets one sharp sentence to prove it should replace the appliance now speaking. The toaster, blender, fridge, and oven are not exchanging compliments; they are cross-examining one another with heat, force, cold, and timing.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new appliance directly defeats the previous appliance's active job by stopping, reversing, or overpowering it; merely avoiding its reach, enduring it, or choosing a larger appliance loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name the appliance and the job it shuts down: "I am the freezer, stopping the oven's cooking by locking the food in ice." A bigger copy is rejected: "I am a giant oven" only turns up the same heat.
sketches.first_card: I am the toaster, springing bread into heat.

sketches.title: Knife-and-Fork Court
sketches.premise: Kitchen tools stand trial in a grand courtroom. Each turn, summon one tool that defeats the previous tool's task, not by being vaguely stronger but by making that task impossible, pointless, or finished.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks for a direct tool-versus-tool counter such as cutting rope, gripping a knife, sweeping crumbs, or washing grease away; dodging, surviving, using a larger version, or naming a related tool without a different counter loses.
sketches.move_shape: State the tool, its action, and the target: "I am the tongs, gripping the fork so it cannot stab the food." A cousin is not enough: "I am a spoon" does not automatically defeat a fork.
sketches.first_card: I am a chef's knife, slicing a carrot into obedient little coins.

sketches.title: Spill Response
sketches.premise: A kitchen disaster escalates one response at a time: stain, puddle, grease, smoke, fire, and stranger messes demand the next concrete cleanup or control. The player who offers a response that cannot actually handle the standing mess gets theatrically swept off the floor.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new standing response directly contains, absorbs, scrapes, washes, smothers, cools, or safely removes the previous kitchen mess; sidestepping it, merely enduring it, or offering a bigger version of the same mess loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name the response and its physical result: "I am a towel, soaking up the spilled milk." A bigger copy fails: "I am a bigger spill" is not cleanup, just milk with delusions.
sketches.first_card: A puddle of orange juice spreads beneath the fridge.

sketches.title: Pantry Chain
sketches.premise: Players name pantry items in a chain where each new item makes the previous one unable to serve its purpose. The pantry is a battlefield of taste, texture, and storage: salt can spoil a sweet mix, water can dissolve sugar, and a hungry eater can end the whole affair.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new item plainly spoils, dissolves, mixes away, seals, consumes, or otherwise makes the previous item fail as food or pantry stock; dodging contact, surviving unchanged, or using a bigger or same-family item loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one pantry thing and its direct effect: "I am water, dissolving the sugar into syrup." A cousin fails: "I am brown sugar" is still sugar wearing a darker coat.
sketches.first_card: A bowl of dry sugar, sparkling on the pantry shelf.
